inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,797 Python-split logical lines of the normalized article. The source is mathematically coherent despite formula-layout risk and six control-character line breaks in lines 1199-1334. It develops two linked RH-conditional measurements for zeros of zeta derivatives: a weighted real-part sum and an unweighted counting formula. Its reusable mechanisms are the replacement of unavailable logarithmic-derivative structure by separately controlled holomorphic logarithmic branches, Littlewood-lemma rectangle decompositions, Jensen/Cauchy argument bounds, epsilon optimization near the critical line, and endpoint perturbation. Formula typography is sometimes flattened, but the checked prose and displayed-equation neighborhoods recover the selected mechanisms.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Branch engineering replaces unavailable logarithmic-derivative structure
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: When a higher derivative ratio is not itself a logarithmic derivative, prove nonvanishing and sector bounds for factors separately, normalize their logarithms on overlapping regions, and account for the residual integer branch offset by continuity.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Established here only in RH-dependent zero-free regions for the specific F and zeta derivative factors; it is not a general branch-existence theorem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Wide and thin Littlewood rectangles extract complementary zero statistics
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A fixed-width rectangle retains beta weights and exposes an integrated argument error, while subtraction across a vanishing strip cancels those weights and leaves boundary arguments that count zeros.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Both conversions depend on admissible zero-free horizontal boundaries and the chosen logarithmic branches.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The critical-line buffer is a tunable bridge between local growth and global contour error
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Jensen/Cauchy bounds deteriorate with distance from the critical line, so splitting the contour and optimizing an explicit buffer converts local analytic growth estimates into the final log-log error scale.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The optimized rate is conditional on the cited RH bounds and on this solver's available estimate for arg G_k.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The formal main term is not the practical bottleneck
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: After exact contour bookkeeping supplies the main asymptotics, progress is controlled by a boundary-argument estimate—especially arg G_k—rather than by further manipulation of the main term.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a source-specific diagnosis under RH; the paper explicitly lacks quantitative information about the implied constant.
